newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Congress seen favoring vote on re-election.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Congress seen favoring vote on re-election.

text.p: Nearly half of Brazil's lower house of Congress would support a national referendum to decide whether to allow President Fernando Henrique Cardoso to run for an unprecedented second term, a poll published on Saturday said.

Some 47.3 percent of Brazil's Chamber of Deputies agreed to a referendum on the controversial re-election issue, while 40.5 percent felt the matter should be decided by lawmakers, according to the poll by Folha de Sao Paulo newspaper.
The remaining 12.2 percent were undecided. Folha did not give a margin of error for the poll, which surveyed 488 of the chamber's 513 deputies this week.
Brazil banned re-election of executive office holders when it became a republic in 1889 in reaction to the authoritarian colonial rule it saw under the Portuguese monarchy.
But Cardoso hopes to follow his South American counterparts, Peru's Alberto Fujimori and Carlos Menem in Argentina, who were able to rewrite their nations' constitutions to permit re-election.

Brazil's lower house was scheduled to begin a first round of voting next week on a bill that would allow Cardoso to run in the 1998 presidential election. Supporters of re-election argue that the continuity of a second Cardoso term would ensure the long-term success of economic reforms that have slashed inflation during his first term.
Many of Cardoso's detractors say they do not oppose re-election in principle, but say it should not not take effect until after Cardoso's term ends in December 1998.
